A single-slice classification cannot assess growth rate or tumour grade, and therefore cannot provide a definitive assessment of the lesion's significance [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. Clinical and neurological examination, dedicated contrast-enhanced MRI using a brain-tumour protocol, specialist review and, where appropriate, histological grading are matters to discuss with a healthcare professional, as these investigations inform management decisions [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls] [nci-meningioma]. Management decisions depend on tumour location, size, symptoms, growth characteristics, histological grade and the patient's overall condition, with options that may include observation with serial imaging, surgical intervention, radiation-based approaches or supportive care, all of which are specialist decisions after diagnostic confirmation [nci-meningioma] [icom-meningioma-consensus]. Ongoing follow-up typically involves specialist review, interval imaging to monitor growth, comparison with prior studies and reassessment if new neurological symptoms develop [nci-meningioma] [icom-meningioma-consensus].
